name: Territory of Nauru
alt: Nauru Island (League of Nations mandate and UN trust territory)

predecessors.name: German New Guinea
predecessors.text: Nauru: annexed by Germany in 1888 and, on the Nauru page, 'incorporated ... into the Marshall Islands Protectorate'; the History of Nauru page says it was 'incorporated into Germany's New Guinea…

successors.name: Nauru
successors.text: the Republic of Nauru, independent on 31 January 1968

ledger.x: 1920: Nauru passes from the war occupation to the mandate: Australian troops 'held control until 1920' (History of Nauru); 'the terms of the League of Nations mandate were drawn up in 1920' (Nauru).
1942: Japan occupies Nauru: 'Japanese troops occupied Nauru on 25 August 1942' (Nauru); the History of Nauru page gives 26 August 1942.

1945: the Japanese occupation ends: 'Nauru was finally taken back from the Japanese on 13 September 1945' (Nauru); on that day Captain Soeda surrendered the island to Australian forces (History of Nauru).

1947: the mandate becomes a trust territory: 'a trusteeship was established by the United Nations' in 1947, with the UK, Australia and New Zealand as joint administering authority and Australia exercising the administration in practice.

1968: Nauru becomes independent: 'Nauru was granted unconditional independence on 31 January 1968' and 'became the world's smallest independent republic' under President Hammer DeRoburt (History of Nauru).

certainty.note: A single island; the border is the coast.
